specs.anchorText: Semantic segmentation asks the finest spatial question we can pose to a vision model
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft palette on a clean white background: a friendly cartoon robot stands in front of a photo of a sunny street scene and, instead of shouting one label at the whole picture, it gently hands a tiny colored name-tag sticker to each individual pixel of the image, which is drawn as a grid of small square tiles. A few tiles near the robot are happily holding up their little colored tags (green for grass, blue for sky, orange for a car). The robot has a kind expression and a magnifying glass. Composition is calm and uncluttered, generous white margins, expressive and approachable like an XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt textbook figure. No text or lettering anywhere in the image. One clear visual metaphor: a label for every single pixel.
specs.alt: A friendly robot hands a small colored name tag to every individual pixel tile of a street-scene photo, with sky tiles getting blue tags, grass tiles green, and a car tile orange, illustrating that semantic segmentation assigns a class to every location instead of one label for the whole image.
specs.caption: Classification shouts one word at the whole picture; segmentation sits down and gives every single pixel a label of its own.

specs.anchorText: U-Net wires a skip at every level, so detail is reinjected continuously
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft palette on a clean white background: a U-shaped valley drawn as a smooth letter-U slope. On the left side, a cartoon hiker (a friendly character) walks downhill carrying a big heavy backpack labeled with abstract shapes, and as they descend they keep dropping small sparkling detail-crystals onto ledges. On the right side, climbing back up, the character is helped by horizontal ropes stretched straight across the U from each left ledge to the matching right ledge, each rope carrying one of the dropped sparkling crystals back to the same height. The crystals represent fine spatial detail being handed back across the U at every level. Gentle, encouraging mood, one clear metaphor, minimal clutter, generous margins. No text or lettering in the image.
specs.alt: A character descends the left arm of a U-shaped valley dropping sparkling detail crystals on each ledge, then climbs the right arm while horizontal ropes carry each crystal straight across to the matching height, depicting how U-Net skip connections reinject the encoder's fine spatial detail into the decoder at every resolution level.
specs.caption: Pooling drops the fine detail on the way down; skip connections are the ropes that hand it straight back at every level on the way up.

specs.anchorText: The entire RoIAlign contribution can be summarized as
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft palette on a clean white background, split into two gentle side-by-side panels. Left panel: a cartoon character tries to trace the outline of a fish that sits at a fractional position on a grid of square tiles, but is forced to snap a cut-out rectangle to the nearest whole tile lines, so the cut-out floats slightly off the fish and the edges miss; the character looks mildly frustrated. Right panel: a calm confident character keeps the fish exactly where it is and reads values smoothly between the grid lines using little dots placed at in-between positions, so the cut-out hugs the fish perfectly. Friendly expressions, clear contrast between misaligned and aligned, minimal clutter, generous margins. No text or lettering in the image.
specs.alt: Two side-by-side panels: on the left a character snaps a crop rectangle to the nearest whole grid cells so it floats off the fish it is trying to cut out, and on the right a character keeps the region exactly in place and reads values at in-between sample points so the crop hugs the fish, illustrating how RoIAlign replaces RoIPool's coordinate rounding with bilinear sampling.
specs.caption: Two innocent round() calls were shifting every crop off its object; RoIAlign just stops rounding, because masks live and die by the half-pixel.

specs.anchorText: Think of the 100 queries as 100 interns sent to find objects
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft palette on a clean white background: a busy but tidy scene of many small identical friendly cartoon intern characters (drawn as little rounded helpers, about a dozen shown to suggest a larger crowd) sent out across a single shared photo of a simple scene. Each intern lassoes or gently outlines one region and proudly holds up a small colored cut-out shape of the thing it claimed (one grabs a cat shape, one a tree shape, one a patch of sky). Several other interns stand to the side shrugging cheerfully with empty hands, having honestly found nothing. The mood is light and cooperative. One clear metaphor: a fixed set of queries each claim one mask, and unused ones report no object. Minimal clutter, generous margins. No text or lettering in the image.
specs.alt: A crowd of small identical intern characters fan out over one shared scene, each lassoing and holding up a colored cut-out of the single region it claimed while several shrug with empty hands having found nothing, depicting Mask2Former's fixed set of learnable queries that each predict one mask and class, with unused queries reporting no object.
specs.caption: Instead of filling in a label grid cell by cell, a fixed crew of queries each go claim one region; the honest ones with nothing to find simply report no object.

specs.anchorText: SAM is class-agnostic: every mask it returns is pure foreground-versus-background geometry
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft palette on a clean white background: a friendly cartoon robot with scissors-for-hands cheerfully cuts a clean outline around an unusual object it has clearly never seen before (a quirky piece of coral or an odd machine part). A human hand simply points one finger at the object. Above the robot's head is an empty thought bubble with just a question mark, showing it does not know the object's name yet still cuts the perfect boundary. The robot looks happy and unbothered. One clear metaphor: you do not need a name to find an edge. Minimal clutter, generous margins, gentle inclusive humor. No text or lettering in the image.
specs.alt: A cheerful robot with scissor hands neatly cuts the outline of an unfamiliar coral-like object that a human finger simply points at, while an empty thought bubble holding only a question mark shows the robot has no name for the object, illustrating SAM's class-agnostic promptable segmentation that outlines whatever you indicate without knowing what it is.
specs.caption: Point at anything, even an object no dataset ever named, and SAM still cuts a clean edge: it turns out you do not need a word for something to find its boundary.

specs.anchorText: a model that predicts "background" everywhere scores 95 percent accuracy while segmenting nothing
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm soft palette on a clean white background: a smug, lazy cartoon student-robot has painted an entire exam sheet a single flat background color, completely ignoring a tiny important object in the corner. It proudly holds up a report card showing a big high grade (drawn as a large filled star or gold ribbon, no letters). Standing next to it, a kindly teacher character holding a magnifying glass points sternly at the tiny missed object, with a small disappointed-but-fair expression. One clear metaphor: a high pixel-accuracy score that hides a model that found nothing. Gentle humor, not mean. Minimal clutter, generous margins. No text or lettering in the image.
specs.alt: A smug lazy student robot has colored an entire exam sheet one flat background shade while ignoring a tiny object in the corner, yet proudly displays a high gold-star grade, as a teacher with a magnifying glass points at the missed object, illustrating the pixel-accuracy trap where predicting background everywhere scores high accuracy yet near-zero mean IoU.
specs.caption: Predict background everywhere and you can ace pixel accuracy while finding nothing at all; if a metric rewards that, it is not measuring segmentation, which is why mean IoU sits at the top of every leaderboard.
